modules.name: Trusted Types sink coverage
modules.description: Maps whether Trusted Types exists and how classic HTML/script sinks behave under the current policy environment.
modules.securityNote: Trusted Types is one of the strongest defenses for DOM XSS, but coverage differs by browser and by sink. This probe inventories the boundary without executing attacker code.

modules.name: Sanitizer and safe HTML API surface
modules.description: Checks emerging HTML sanitization and safe-set APIs that change how defensive code should treat markup.
modules.securityNote: The Sanitizer API and setHTML-style methods affect whether apps need custom sanitizers. Partial implementations can create portability traps.

modules.name: DOM clobbering named properties
modules.description: Creates named elements and records which identifiers become visible through document or window named property lookup.
modules.securityNote: DOM clobbering is still a common way to subvert assumptions in client-side code that trusts globals or document properties.

modules.name: Window and realm entrypoints
modules.description: Enumerates references that resolve to the active Window or expose neighboring browsing contexts.
modules.securityNote: Many browser bugs begin with the wrong assumption about which realm, WindowProxy, or browsing context a value belongs to.

modules.name: MessageEvent mutability
modules.description: Checks whether selected postMessage event fields are writable, configurable, or fixed by the browser.
modules.securityNote: postMessage bugs often come from trusting event shape, source, or origin checks. This probe maps descriptor behavior.

modules.name: URL canonicalization traps
modules.description: Feeds suspicious but inert URL strings into the browser URL parser and records normalization behavior.
modules.securityNote: URL allowlists fail when app code and browser navigation disagree about host, path, username, or scheme normalization.

modules.name: Parser inertness matrix
modules.description: Compares how inert parsing surfaces preserve scripts, event handler attributes, templates, SVG, and MathML.
modules.securityNote: Sanitizers, preview renderers, and import pipelines often parse markup in one context and later move nodes into another.

test.fuzzData: x

modules.name: Declarative Shadow DOM parsing
modules.description: Checks parser behavior for declarative shadow roots and related template attributes.
modules.securityNote: Declarative Shadow DOM changes how server-rendered components and sanitizers need to reason about hidden subtree boundaries.

modules.name: Isolation and capability state
modules.description: Detects APIs gated by cross-origin isolation, secure contexts, or permission policy.
modules.securityNote: High-resolution timers, SharedArrayBuffer, and related APIs depend on isolation headers and permissions that are easy to misconfigure.

modules.name: Storage partitioning probe
modules.description: Checks storage, cache, and access APIs that reveal privacy partitioning and third-party boundary behavior.
modules.securityNote: Storage partitioning affects CSRF assumptions, tracking defenses, embedded widgets, and cache-based bug classes.

modules.name: Cookie prefix boundary check
modules.description: Attempts harmless writes for modern cookie prefixes and records whether the browser accepts, rejects, or blocks access.
modules.securityNote: __Host and __Secure prefix rules are only useful when apps deploy them correctly and browsers enforce the expected constraints.

modules.name: Navigation API and URL state
modules.description: Checks modern navigation primitives that can reshape routing, history, and URL validation assumptions.
modules.securityNote: Client routers and security filters increasingly interact with Navigation API, URLPattern, BFCache, and history state.

modules.name: Capability API inventory
modules.description: Surveys powerful APIs that should be permission-gated, secure-context-gated, or policy-gated.
modules.securityNote: Unexpected API exposure is often the first clue in permission-policy, secure-context, or embedding bugs.

modules.name: CSSOM injection surfaces
modules.description: Exercises CSS parsing APIs that can matter for style injection, selector confusion, and data exposure classes.
modules.securityNote: CSS injection is not JavaScript execution, but it still matters for UI redress, data-dependent styling, and policy bypasses.

modules.name: Prototype pollution gadget survey
modules.description: Checks whether selected DOM-facing option bags inherit values that app code may accidentally trust.
modules.securityNote: Prototype pollution becomes exploitable when option bags and DOM APIs consume inherited values in surprising ways.

modules.name: Structured clone brand checks
modules.description: Tests how structuredClone handles modern platform objects and where cloning boundaries throw.
modules.securityNote: postMessage, workers, IndexedDB, and caches all lean on structured cloning. Brand checks are security boundaries.

modules.name: Wasm and compile boundaries
modules.description: Checks WebAssembly parser availability and compile behavior for minimal byte sequences.
modules.securityNote: Wasm availability intersects with CSP, cross-origin isolation, and JIT hardening decisions.

modules.name: Scheduler and timing primitives
modules.description: Inventories modern scheduling APIs that affect race windows, XS-Leak timing, and task ordering.
modules.securityNote: Task ordering and timer precision still matter for race-condition bugs and cross-site leak research.

modules.name: Import map and module boundaries
modules.description: Checks module-era features that influence script resolution and supply-chain assumptions.
modules.securityNote: Import maps, speculation rules, and modulepreload can change where code comes from and how security scanners reason about script entrypoints.
